data.long_meaning: The name Jean is derived from the Hebrew name 'Yehohanan' which means 'God is gracious'. The Greek form is Ioannes, which was commonly used in the New Testament. She claimed to have divine messages from saints, dressing in masculine attire and leading the French army to several important victories, including the relief of Orléans in 1429.

Saint Jeanne de Chateau-Thierry, also known as Joan of Arc of the Blessed Sacrament, was a French Catholic saint who lived in the 17th century. Born in Dijon, she experienced visions and ecstasies from a very young age, and was known for her devotion to the Blessed Sacrament. She spent most of her life as a hermit in a small cell in the chapel of a monastery in Chateau-Thierry, where she received countless visitors.
